goals: Compare corresponding triangle measurements including attachment of marked side to specific angle vertices.
Distinguish identical copies after rotation/reflection from differently sized/arranged triangles.
Do not require memorization of formal ASA/SAS/SSS criteria at this stage.

sourceTasks.source: Observe and contrast six triangle figures in Set 1 and four in Set 2; identify identical versus different shapes.
sourceTasks.coverage: Existing Rich V2 SSS/AAA mathematical examples retained and language repaired for physical overlay; original 6+4 publisher images not recreated.

sourceTasks.source: Compare nine figures and justify how many genuinely different triangles, taking side–angle adjacency into account.
sourceTasks.coverage: Explanation now requires checking correspondence, including whether angle is between named sides; not claiming parity for all nine publisher triangles.

sourceTasks.source: Compare eight triangles; show how the same three numerical measurements could make distinct triangles when the marked side has another adjacency.
sourceTasks.coverage: Original SVG shows 40°, 60°, and length 5 once as AB and once as AC; noncongruent despite identical numeric measures. Does not reproduce all eight publisher illustrations.

sourceTasks.source: Two triangles each have an angle 32° and side lengths 5 and 6 in different adjacencies; position determines identical-copy classification.
sourceTasks.coverage: New original example changes measurements intentionally to 40°, 60°, length 5, to demonstrate the same general adjacency principle without copying publisher geometry.

model.reason: The 5-unit side belongs to different corresponding vertex pairs, so the whole triangles have different side lengths.

learnerTask: Draw or trace two triangles each with 40° and 60° measured at vertices A and B, and one side of 5 units; first position 5 units on AB, then on AC. Independently measure the remaining sides and overlay figures (allowing rotation/reflection). Explain which corresponding side lengths differ and why the figures cannot be identical copies despite their three shared numerical measurements.

criteria.description: Construct both original triangle models with accurately measured angles and correct, distinct placement of the 5-unit side.
Identify corresponding sides, compare independently measured third-side lengths, and correctly reject congruence.
Explain why a rotation or reflection alone gives an identical triangle but moving the specified side to a different vertex pair changes the constraints.
Give written/oral comparative reasoning and accurately label angles, side units and student measurements; distinguish examples from publisher source figures.

cases.claim: Both figures have 40°,60°,80° but AB=5 in first and AB≈5.686 in second; not identical.
cases.expectation: Correct math; teacher still checks original measured drawings.

cases.claim: Two angles and one side length automatically mean identical triangles, regardless of which side is 5.
A 90° rotation makes a different triangle.
cases.expectation: Reject; a rigid rotation preserves lengths and angles.

cases.claim: Three 40°,60°,80° rays drawn along a single line are a triangle.
Only says 'different' without figure, corresponding measurements or explanation.
cases.expectation: Teacher cannot award full source-task credit.

cases.claim: Mislabels AB and AC on original construction, obscuring which is 5.
cases.expectation: Request correct marked side and vertices.
